book.title: MPFR 4.2.2: the correct-rounding guarantee at precision 53
book.description: MPFR's manual states that the value stored in the destination variable is correctly rounded, for every function and every rounding mode. The claims here are registered with that certified-bound evidence class; each row is a finite-grid conformance check at precision 53, so the rows support the guarantee rather than carry it. The expected value is an independent evaluation at increasing precision certified by mpfr_can_round.

provenance.measurement: wider-validation/mpfr/driver.c; the expected value is computed at 53+64 to 53+16384 bits and certified by mpfr_can_round for each rounding mode
provenance.data: one CSV per function under data/, generated by wider-validation/gen_inputs.py and measured by the driver
provenance.reading: the rows measure precision 53 on a sample in the binary64 normal range; the library's guarantee is the certified bound, and the rows support it

domain.description: all MPFR numbers at precision 53; the rows sample binary64 arguments

the reference is MPFR at higher precision; this is a conformance check, not an independent oracle

registrations.sentence: The value stored in the destination variable is correctly rounded, i.e., MPFR behaves as if it computed the result with an infinite precision, then rounded it to the precision of this variable.
registrations.scope: mpfr_sin at precision 53 and each of the four rounding modes; the manual's guarantee applies to every MPFR function

supporting.sentence: The input variables are regarded as exact (in particular, their precision does not affect the result).

As a consequence, in case of a non-zero real rounded result, the error on the result is less than or equal to 1/2 ulp (unit in the last place) of that result in the rounding to nearest mode, and less than 1 ulp of that result in the directed rounding modes (a ulp is the weight of the least significant represented bit of the result after rounding).
